chapter: Carnivals, Kansas City and the road to Chicago
title: His father's death and his mother's insistence on school
summary: His father died in 1921. He wanted to work to help support his siblings, but his mother made him stay in school, discovering his cement-plant job from the cement in his eyes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anyway, Bill said, 'why don't you go to Chicago?' I said, 'well, man, I don't know how to' -- he said, 'Good as you play, you should be in Chicago.' So we decided that when he went back to Chicago I would go. So I didn't have money, you know, to go like that. Of course, I wanted to go for the very simple reason my mother wouldn't let me work. She wanted me to go to school and I wanted to work and help her support my brother and sister because my father had died when I was 11, in 1921.

But she wouldn't have it. She wanted me to -- in fact, I got a job one time working during this time I was back, I got a job working with the cement plant. And I worked a week and she finally looked at my eyes at suppertime and saw the cement in my eyes. And she said, have you been going to school? And I had to confess. Well, she made me go back to school.
